title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: design custom AI agents with the AI development toolkit
summary: Hold: the briefing reports credit-allocation automation as undocumented, although Microsoft publishes a Power Platform API tutorial for it. It also overstates the task creator's permission ceiling, overlooks published Expense Agent rates, and reports the capability default as unstated despite Microsoft's default-on guidance.

claims.claim: Feature-specific custom-agent credit rates and quota are not yet published.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table; Governance controls prose
claims.claim: No API equivalent of the Business Central Allow data movement toggle is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Allow data movement" "API" "Business Central"; Business Central Copilot agent capabilities activate deactivate API PowerShell Allow data movement configuration. Opened enable-ai and ai-copilot-data-movement; found UI instructions but no toggle API.

claims.claim: The toggle appears only when a capability might process data in a different Azure geography.
claims.quote: The Allow data movement toggle appears when one or more copilot and agent capabilities might process data in a different Azure geography from the Business Central environment.

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly identify whether the general geography toggle applies to Custom Agent.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Central Custom Agent AI development toolkit Allow data movement geography. Opened enable-ai, ai-copilot-data-movement and toolkit overview. General native-agent routing is documented, but no explicit Custom Agent mapping was found.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center capacity path is Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Manage Capacity.
claims.quote: In the Licensing pane, under Products, select Copilot Studio. Select the Summary tab. ... Select Manage Capacity from the Prepaid capacity card.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls table; Governance controls: opening paragraph
claims.claim: No API or automation is documented for environment Copilot Credit capacity allocation.
claims.quote: you can manage Copilot credit allocations with code by using the Power Platform API and the administration (Admin) SDKs.
claims.fix: Replace controls[3].api=null with the documented REST allocation operation: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01, with scope.environmentId, allocatedEntitlements entitlementId MCSMessages and allocation.quantity in the body. Cite this tutorial, preserve its authentication/role requirements and TenantPool enforcement qualification, and remove the UI-only claim from the prose.

claims.claim: Capability changes can be immediate or require users to sign out and back in.
claims.quote: Some AI features take effect immediately, while others require users to sign out and sign in again.

claims.claim: Administrators can monitor prepaid and pay-as-you-go capacity and usage in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: You can view Copilot Credit capacity and usage for prepaid capacity and pay-as-you-go in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Consumed-credit telemetry is emitted to the Application Insights resource configured for the Business Central environment.
claims.quote: telemetry is emitted to the Application Insights resource set up for the environment for Copilot Credits consumed.

claims.claim: Agent definitions can be exported for backup.
claims.quote: The purpose of this feature is to allow you to back up your agent configuration, share it with others, or move it between different sandbox environments.

claims.claim: The roadmap recommends storing exported definitions in source control.
claims.quote: We recommend storing these files in a source control system like GitHub to track changes and maintain version history.

claims.claim: The Business Central assigning-permissions article explains how to grant permission sets to users.
claims.quote: You can assign permissions sets to users in two ways: From the User Card page, by selecting permission sets to assign to the user.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/business-central/ui-define-granular-permissions to sources and link the assigning-permissions reference in this paragraph.

claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to inventory and remove human users' design and diagnostics permission sets, but no control row covers that user access.
claims.quote: Identify which people hold the AGENT - ADMIN and AGENT - DIAGNOSTICS permission sets and remove them from anyone who does not need to design agents.
claims.fix: Add a user-scope row for who may design agents or inspect diagnostics. Use Business Central > Users > user > Edit > User Permission Sets, documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/business-central/ui-define-granular-permissions#to-assign-a-permission-set-on-a-user-card. The existing agent-scope row controls the agent's permissions, not the human designer's.

claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to monitor consumption, but the capacity-allocation row does not show the monitoring control.
claims.quote: Watch Copilot Credit consumption in the Power Platform admin center, and in Application Insights telemetry if it is set up for the environment.
claims.fix: Add a monitoring row using Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Environments > environment > Copilot Credits capacity, citing https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-copilot-studio-copilot-credits-capacity. Note the optional Business Central Application Insights telemetry with the consumption-billing source.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not publish a feature-specific price for the AI development toolkit.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Central Custom Agent AI development toolkit billing events price Copilot Credits. Read the toolkit overview, prerequisites and consumption-billing page; results include generic Copilot Credit prices, not a toolkit-specific price.

claims.quote: If your organization's quota is low or depleted, users receive in-app notifications about the status and necessary actions.

claims.claim: Search (Alt+Q) is the documented entry point to Copilot & agent capabilities.
